_comment: Closes the arc: the question only a cohort can answer, asked at the lesson's close.

stem.en: The plant's medical officer asks you one question: how many of our men fall ill with this tumour each year? Which design answers it?

text.en: A case-control study, because it starts from the men who fell ill
A cohort study, because a group followed forward gives the incidence rate the question asks for
Either design, because in this case both produced the same association
Neither design; the odds ratio of 13.2 read per year is the answer

explanation.en: A rate of new illness per year is an incidence, and incidence needs a counted group of people still well, followed over time: 12 cases among 2,000 reactor men over twenty years gives 6.0 per 1,000 over the follow-up. A case-control study assembles its groups after the outcomes are known and has no such followed group, so it can rank the exposure's strength but cannot produce a rate. The 13.2 is a ratio of odds with no time in it, and reading it per year would be inventing a denominator.

hints.en: The question asks for a count of new illness per head per year. Which design held a group under observation while that count accumulated?
